17-13-0303-C (1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans - Zoning Map Amendment
1429 West Irving Park Road, Chicago, Illinois

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: 15,000 square feet

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is seeking a Type I Zoning Map Amendment, with secondary
relief for Administrative Adjustment and Variation, pursuant to Section 17-
13-0300 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, in order to permit the
redevelopment of the subject property with a new five-story mixed-use
building. The programming for the proposed new development calls for the
establishment of divisible commercial space (+/- 4,400 square feet) at the
front of the ground floor, facing Irving Park Road, and a total of thirty-six
(36) dwelling units, including seven (7) affordable (ARO) units, to be
distributed on and between the 2" through 5" floors. Off-street parking for
a total of twenty-five (25) vehicles and twenty (20) bicycles will be
provided onsite, with fourteen (14) vehicle spaces and all of the bicycle
storage located within the core of the ground floor (attached garage) and
eleven (11) additional vehicular spaces comprising a surface parking pad at
the rear of the building. The proposed improvements will be masonry in
construction and will measure 54 feet-10 inches in height (5 floor ceiling).

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 50,600 square feet *(3.4 FAR)

*The Applicant is eligible for a floor area increase from 3.0 up to 3.5 because they are
providing at least 50% of the required ‘affordable’ units onsite. [Section 17-3-0403-B]

(B) _ The Project’s Density (Lot Area Per Dwelling Unit): 36 units (416.7 square feet)
(C) The amount of off-street parking: *25 automobile spaces; 20 bicycle spaces

*The subject property is located within 2,640 linear feet of the entrance to the Irving
Park Brown Line Line (CTA) Train Station, thereby qualifying as a Transit Served
Location (TSL), under the current Chicago Zoning Ordinance [Section 17-10-0102-B]
and triggering a distinct Parking Standard [Section 17-3-0308] for dwelling units,
which limits the maximum allowable off-street residential parking ratio to 50%. The
new proposed mixed-use building will feature thirty-six (36) dwelling units, at least
eight (8) of which will be three-bedroom units and twenty (20) of which will be two-
bedroom units intended for family occupancy and/or work-from-home dual tenant
occupancy. Applying the TSL Parking Standard results in a maximum by-right
allowance of 18 off-street parking spaces, which was deemed insufficient by community
stakeholders.

Therefore, in consideration of current market demand for larger format rental housing
units with designated off-street parking, as echoed by the community stakeholders, the
Applicant is proposing to increase the number of off-street automobile parking spaces
to serve this transit-oriented development, so that all of the three-bedroom units and
all but three (3) of the two-bedroom units will have designated onsite vehicular parking
accommodations. As such, the Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment - in
conjunction with this Type I Zoning Map Amendment, to increase the maximum
automobile parking ratio for a transit served location (TSL) — from 18 spaces (50%) to
25 spaces (69%). [Section 17-3-0308-B; Section 17-13-1003-EE.]

(D) Setbacks: a. Front Setback: 0 foot-0 inches
b. *Rear Setback: 22 feet-0 inches

c. Side Setbacks:
West: 0 feet-0 inches
East: 0 feet-0 inches

*In order to accommodate the provision of larger format dwelling units intended for
occupancy by growing families that desire the flexibility and financial viability of
renting, which were current market observations specifically echoed during many
months of ongoing community engagement, the Applicant had to amplify the
residential floorplates for the upper floors, allowing for longer layouts, as well as
inset balconies for each unit. Such building orientation and scale is completely
compatible with the pattern of improvements on this mixed-use block, where almost
all of the properties are occupied by buildings that span the entire width and depth of
their respective site - including the immediately adjacent four-story multi-unit
residential complex to the west that was constructed lot line-to-lot line on all four
sides and the adjacent multi-tenant commercial complex to the east that was
constructed without any side or rear setbacks, As such, the Applicant is seeking an
Administrative Adjustment / Variation, to reduce the minimum rear setback for floors
containing dwelling units and/or residential accessory uses from 30 feet-0 inches to
22 feet-0 inches (34% reduction). [Section 17-3-0405-A; Sections(s) 17-13-1003-I;
17-13-1101-B].

(E) Building Height: 54 feet-10 inches (underside of 5” Floor ceiling beam)

COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 17-3-0308
Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations

In all B and C districts, any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail
station entrance must satisfy all of the following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.

The project calls for the construction and occupancy of a new five-story mixed-use
development at the subject property, which qualifies as a Transit-Served Location (TSL) due to its
proximity to the Irving Park CTA Brown Line Train Station. The ground floor of the new proposed
development will feature divisible commercial / retail space occupying and activating the entire
street frontage along Irving Park Road. A total of thirty-six (36) dwelling units will be distributed
on and between the 2" floor through the 5" floors, eight (8) of which will feature three bedrooms
and twenty (20) of which will feature two bedrooms, intended to accommodate growing families
and work-from-home dual tenancy. At the time of filing, the programming also includes the onsite
provision of seven (7) affordable units (ARO) included in the thirty-six, which such units will be
a representative and equal mix of the unit types, quality and orientation of the market rate units.
The design and functionality of the dwelling units were developed in a conscious effort to attract
and provide newly rendered economical rental housing for families and/or work-from-home
dwellers, so to ensure ongoing activation of the property from ground up and to add more vested
members to the immediate community, who will patronize and help to revitalize the existing
businesses, while the inclusion of the newly rendered commercial / retail space(s) is intended to
encourage interest from local businesses / entrepreneurs and/or service providers seeking to
support the residents and occupants of the neighborhood while also complimenting the other well-
established businesses in the area. Rounding out the development is onsite / off-street parking for
a total of twenty-five (25) vehicles, fourteen (14) of which such corresponding spaces will be
located within the interior of the building behind the commercial / retail spaces, while the other
eleven (11) spaces will comprise a surface parking pad at the rear and outside of the new building,
so that all such onsite parking accommodations are completely concealed from the adjacent public
ways in full compliance with the Pedestrian Street Design Standards & Guidelines. Several of
both the interior and exterior parking stalls will be equipped with electric (EVSE) charging
stations, in an effort to further reduce the carbon footprint of the new development, while allowing
most of the residents the opportunity and security of having one personal vehicle, actively
mitigating private consumption of the limited public parking facilities in the neighborhood and
further advancing the City’s land use and planning policies. In addition hereto, and in furtherance
of these sustainable policies and goals, the new development also accommodates enclosed parking
and storage for at least twenty (20) bicycles, e-bicycles, scooters and/or strollers. Such proposed
parking provisions represents a 69% automobile-to-unit ratio and a 55% bicycle-to-unit ratio, so
that the residents of all but one of the units will be designated their own off-street vehicular parking
space, thereby promoting options and increased reliance on the many other meaningful multi-
modal forms of nearby public transit and environmentally conscious transportation.

(NTRO DATE
OCT 14,202

ORDINANCE

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY OF CHICAGO - CITY COUNCIL:

SECTION 1. Title 17, of the Municipal Code of Chicago, the Chicago Zoning
Ordinance be amended by changing all the B3-2 Community Shopping District symbols
and indications as shown on Map Grid Index No. 9-G in the area bounded by

West Irving Park Road; a line 135 feet east of North Janssen Avenue; the

alley next south of and parallel to Irving Park Road; a line 35 feet east of

North Janssen Avenue
to those of an B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District.

SECTION 2. This ordinance shall be in force and effect from and after its

passage and due publication.

Common Address: 1429 West Irving Park Road, Chicago, Illinois
